shared_elements: standing frontal human figure carved in relief on stone
elaborate headdress/headgear with vertical elements at top
circular disc or medallion at the centre of the torso
arms bent with hands meeting across the chest/waist
stone monument with weathered, eroded surface
vertically stacked composition (head/headdress, torso, lower body)
curving band or belt-like element across the lower body
justification: Both are relief-carved stone monuments showing a frontal standing figure organised in the same vertical order — broad headdress on top, torso with a prominent central round disc or boss, arms folded in across the middle, and a belt-like band above the lower body — which is a fairly specific shared scheme. The rendering differs sharply, however: A is a tall, thin slab covered in fine, dense, small-scale ornament and glyph-like panels, while B is a squat, boulder-like mass with few, broad, deeply cut and simplified forms, and the two photographs (grainy black-and-white outdoor versus colour museum interior) reinforce the very different overall impression.
